The petitioner has challenged the investigation launched against her in Cr.No.37/2017 by respondent No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 494, 496, 506, 498A, 323, 324 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code, (henceforth referred to as 'IPC' for short) pending trial before II Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Tumkur.

sentences.text: 2. An information about commission of cognizable offence was reported by respondent No.2 with respondent No.1 on 24.04.2017 which disclosed that the respondent No.2 was given in marriage to the accused No.1 on 23.02.2003.
She claimed that from the marriage, she had two children named Amith A.N and Dhanush A.N.
She alleged that accused No.1 had physically and mentally abused her for more dowry and attempts by the well-wishers to drive sense into the petitioner proved futile.
Later accused No.1 disowned her and her children NC: 2023:KHC:29497 and threw her out of the house.
She claimed that she was residing with her mother at N.S.Puram, Tumakuru.
She alleged that the accused No.1 used to frequently visit her mother's house and from February, 2017, he had stopped going there.
Later, she enquired and found that the accused No.1 had contracted a second marriage with the accused No.2/petitioner herein.

When she went to the house where the accused No.1 and petitioner were residing, she found both of them in the house and when she confronted them, accused No.1 disclosed that he had married accused No.2/petitioner and that he threatened to kill her, if she disclosed it to anybody.
Later accused No.1 and petitioner held respondent No.2 by her hair and assaulted her and that petitioner herein brought out a knife and attempted to kill her.

Based on this, jurisdictional police registered Cr.No.37/2017 for the offences punishable under Sections 494, 496, 506, 498A, 323, 324 read with 34 of IPC and launched an investigation which is challenged in this petition.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner cannot be accused of an offence punishable under Section 494 of IPC.

Insofar as the other allegations are NC: 2023:KHC:29497 concerned, he contended that it did not constitute an offence under Sections 323 or 324 of IPC, as there is no injury on the body of the respondent No.2.

Further it is contended that respondent No.2 had admittedly gone to the house of petitioner and created a commotion and therefore, her allegation that she was assaulted is without any basis and cannot be believed.
Therefore, he contended that an offence under Section 506 of IPC is also not made.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent No.2 on the other hand submitted that there are overt-acts mentioned in the complaint which indicates that the petitioner had brought out a knife with an intention to kill the respondent No.2 and therefore, though an offence under Section 494 of IPC is not maintainable against the petitioner, but yet, there are sufficient material to indicate the commission of offences under Sections 323, 324 and 506 of IPC and therefore, proceedings cannot be quashed.
5. I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
An offence under Section 494 of IPC is said to be committed against spouse who during the subsistence of a marriage, had married another person.
It therefore follows that the person married cannot be accused of an offence punishable under Section 494 of IPC.
In the present case, it is alleged by respondent No.2 that the petitioner/accused No.2 was the second wife of accused No.1.
Therefore, the petitioner cannot be prosecuted for an offence under Section 494 of IPC.

For the sake of immediate reference Section 494 of IPC is extracted below:
"494. Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife.- Whoever, having a husband or wife living, marries in any case in which such marriage is void by reason of its taking place during the life of such husband or wife, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

Exception.-This section does not extend to any person whose marriage with such husband or wife has been declared void by a Court of competent jurisdiction, nor to any person who contracts a marriage during the life of a former husband or wife, if such husband or wife, at the time of the subsequent marriage, shall have been continually absent from such person for the NC: 2023:KHC:29497 space of seven years, and shall not have been heard of by such person as being alive within that time provided the person contracting such subsequent marriage shall, before such marriage takes place, inform the person with whom such marriage is contracted of the real state of facts so far as the same are within his or her knowledge."
7. Similarly, an offence under Section 496 of IPC can also be pursued only against an erring spouse and not against any other person.
Therefore, the registration of Cr.No.37/2017 for the offences against accused No.2/petitioner for the offences under Sections 494 and 496 IPC deserves to be quashed.

8. Insofar as the allegations that the petitioner/accused No.2 had attempted to stab the respondent No.2, it is to be noticed that the respondent No.2 had gone to the house of petitioner/accused No.2 and a scuffle happened between petitioner and respondent No.2.
The respondent No.2 was not subjected to any medical examination and it is not her case too that she was injured in the incident.

sentences.text: Therefore, there is no basis for an offence under Sections 323 and 324 of IPC.
Even otherwise, the respondent No.2 having gone to the house of petitioner/respondent No.2 cannot justify the commission of an offence by the petitioner punishable under Sections 506 of IPC.
Even if some injury was caused, it could at the most be considered as a harm, which is not punishable under Section 95 of IPC.
Consequently the proceedings against the petitioner/accused No.2 cannot be continued.

Consequently, this petition is allowed and the impugned prosecution of the petitioner for the offences under Sections 494, 496, 506, 323, 324, 498A read with Section 34 of IPC in Cr.No.37/2017 pending trial before the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Tumkur is quashed qua petitioner.
However, proceedings shall continue against the accused No.1.
